pages.lesson:
LESSON: GUIDED WRITING: IMAGINATIVE COMPOSITION

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: ARABIC
Strand: Writing 3.3 Guided writing (2 sessions) • Vocabulary building- animals and birds
Topic 3.5: Guided Writing: Imaginative Composition

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Guided Writing: Imaginative Composition. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How can one develop a creative story?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. construct sentences using acquired vocabulary for comprehension
2. create a short personal and imaginative composition for comprehension
3. appreciate different Arabic writing styles

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: GUIDED WRITING: IMAGINATIVE COMPOSITION
Subject: ARABIC · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Guided Writing: Imaginative Composition helps you succeed in ARABIC. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: GUIDED WRITING: IMAGINATIVE COMPOSITION
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Construct sentences using acquired vocabulary for comprehension

What this means
In this part you learn to construct sentences using acquired vocabulary for comprehension. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: construct sentences using acquired vocabulary for comprehension.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Guided Writing: Imaginative Composition”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can construct sentences using acquired vocabulary for comprehension. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Create a short personal and imaginative composition for comprehension

What this means
In this part you learn to create a short personal and imaginative composition for comprehension. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: create a short personal and imaginative composition for comprehension.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Guided Writing: Imaginative Composition to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can create a short personal and imaginative composition for comprehension. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate different Arabic writing styles

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate different Arabic writing styles. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate different Arabic writing styles.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate different Arabic writing styles. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Guided Writing: Imaginative Composition is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Guided Writing: Imaginative Composition”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: construct sentences using acquired vocabulary for comprehension)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Guided Writing: Imaginative Composition to a partner. (skill: create a short personal and imaginative composition for comprehension)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: appreciate different Arabic writing styles)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Guided Writing: Imaginative Composition to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: construct sentences using acquired vocabulary for comprehension.
3. Practise this skill: create a short personal and imaginative composition for comprehension.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate different Arabic writing styles.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Guided Writing: Imaginative Composition from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Guided Writing: Imaginative Composition: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Guided Writing: Imaginative Composition?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can one develop a creative story?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Guided Writing: Imaginative Composition means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: construct sentences using acquired vocabulary for comprehension.
5. Be able to: create a short personal and imaginative composition for comprehension.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
